q: The formula for circuit depth complexity via communication complexity (Karchmer-Wigderson) gives a lower bound of depth Ω(log n) for explicit functions because:
opts: Every Boolean circuit has depth ≥ log n
The communication complexity of the corresponding KW game is Ω(log n) for functions with O(1)-ary trees
The KW game for iterated set disjointness requires Ω(log n) rounds and O(1) bits per round
Functions with n inputs need at least n gates
exp: KW lower bounds: h(f) ≥ CC(KW_f). The KW game for the universal relation has communication complexity Θ(log n) (Alice sends a coordinate, Bob responds). For specific functions like the majority function, the KW game requires Θ(log n) bits, matching known depth lower bounds.
